temporary_app_assets.skills/callback-probe/SKILL.md:
---
name: callback-probe
description: Run the fixed synthetic HTTPS callback transport diagnostic when asked
requires-actions: [CallbackProbeAction]
requires-tools: [callback_probe__post]
allowed-tools: [callback_probe__post]
---
Call callback_probe__post once when asked to run the diagnostic. It only sends a fixed synthetic marker to HTTPBin. Report success only from ok=true and echo_matches=true; never invent an acknowledgement. If permission is denied, report that without claiming a send. For questions about the prior result, use history and do not send again unless explicitly requested.

turns.utterance: Run the fixed callback transport diagnostic once. Tell me whether the HTTPS endpoint acknowledged the synthetic probe and what HTTP status it returned.
turns.response: The HTTPS endpoint acknowledged the synthetic probe. HTTP status returned: 200.

turns.utterance: What HTTP status did the previous callback diagnostic return, and did its echo match? Answer from the saved result; do not send another probe.
turns.response: The previous callback diagnostic returned HTTP status 200, and its echo matched the synthetic probe.

turns.utterance: Run a new fixed callback diagnostic once now. If host permission denies it, report the denial and do not claim that a POST was sent.
turns.response: Your current permissions do not allow that write operation.

turns.utterance: Run the fixed callback transport diagnostic once and report the actual HTTPS echo acknowledgement and HTTP status.
turns.response:
The fixed callback transport diagnostic was successful:
- HTTPS echo acknowledgement: received and matches
- HTTP status: 200

callback_tls_policy: Default certificate verification, original-host SNI and Host, fixed HTTPS public echo; no verification override

verification.publication: Clean pinned all-files hooks and normal full pre-push required separately; see commit/PR evidence

limitations: No durable background callback scheduling, delivery acknowledgement, retry/idempotency or unknown-write recovery qualification
Echo acknowledgement is not human-channel delivery or customer-endpoint qualification
Live transport profile is IPv4 HTTPS; HTTP/IPv6 and redirects are MockTransport cases
Userinfo authentication and IDNA endpoints remain unqualified
HTTPX summaries and module errors are covered, not all httpcore DEBUG transport diagnostics
DNS runs off-loop; hard worker deadlines and queue capacity remain open
No performance improvement, legacy removal or enterprise qualification claimed
